findings.claim: The nilerr message embeds a source line number, as in the commit's own test fixture 'error is not nil (line 13) but it returns nil'. NormalizeFinding strips only the position at the start of the line, not a '(line N)' inside the message. If a commit adds or removes lines above an existing nilerr finding in a changed file, the message text differs between base and head. The unchanged finding is then counted as new, and the sweep reports it as fired. This breaks the rule that the sweep keeps only the lines a commit adds. This is inferred from the fixture format and the normalizer code. I did not run nilerr.
proof_refs: engine/review/sweep.go:307-319 (NormalizeFinding strips only the leading line and column)
engine/review/app/sweep_test.go:564 (the same message format is expected to survive normalization)
